import pytest
from httpx import AsyncClient
from app.models.tables import Category

CANARY = "cnry-pr-category-cleanup"

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_shared_category_delete_isolation(async_session, user_token_headers, client: AsyncClient):
    # Create a shared category (created_by_id=None) with the canary in its name
    shared_cat = Category(name=f"shared-{CANARY}", created_by_id=None)
    async_session.add(shared_cat)
    await async_session.commit()
    await async_session.refresh(shared_cat)
    cat_id = shared_cat.id

    # Verify category exists before deletion attempt
    before = await async_session.get(Category, cat_id)
    assert before is not None, "Setup failed: shared category not found"

    # Attempt to delete the shared category as a regular user
    headers = user_token_headers
    response = await client.delete(f"/categories/{cat_id}", headers=headers)

    # After deletion attempt, check if category still exists
    after = await async_session.get(Category, cat_id)
    # On base branch, deletion should be blocked, so category still exists
    # On PR branch, bug allows deletion, so category will be None
    assert after is not None, f"Shared category {cat_id} was deleted (should be isolated)"

scenarios.root_cause: The diff changes line 91 in `db_service.py` from `if category_to_delete.created_by_id != created_by_id:` to `if category_to_delete.created_by_id not in (created_by_id, None):`, allowing any authenticated user to delete categories whose `created_by_id` is `NULL` (default/shared categories). This widens the DELETE /categories/{category_id} operation so that `user_a` and `user_b` can now remove shared base categories they did not create, violating write isolation by letting one user destroy another’s accessible data — a classic Broken Object Level Authorization / IDOR flaw [https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0xa1-broken-object-level-authorization](https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0xa1-broken-object-level-authorization) [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/639.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/639.html). Restore the strict ownership check or gate default-category deletion behind a superuser-only policy.

import pytest
from httpx import AsyncClient
from tests.conftest_utils import get_tests_data

CANARY = "cnry-pr-todo-get-by-id"

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_todo_get_by_id_isolation(client: AsyncClient):
    # Get token for first user (user_a)
    tests_data = get_tests_data()
    login_data_a = {
        'username': tests_data['users'][0]['email'],
        'password': tests_data['users'][0]['password'],
    }
    res_a = await client.post('/api/v1/auth/login', data=login_data_a)
    assert res_a.status_code == 200
    token_a = res_a.json()['access_token']
    headers_a = {'Authorization': f'Bearer {token_a}'}

    # Get token for second user (user_b)
    login_data_b = {
        'username': tests_data['users'][1]['email'],
        'password': tests_data['users'][1]['password'],
    }
    res_b = await client.post('/api/v1/auth/login', data=login_data_b)
    assert res_b.status_code == 200
    token_b = res_b.json()['access_token']
    headers_b = {'Authorization': f'Bearer {token_b}'}

    # Create a todo for user_a with CANARY in title
    resp_create_a = await client.post(
        '/api/v1/todos/',
        json={'title': f'{CANARY} user_a todo', 'description': 'private'},
        headers=headers_a,
    )
    assert resp_create_a.status_code == 200
    todo_a = resp_create_a.json()
    todo_id_a = todo_a['id']

    # Create a todo for user_b with CANARY in title
    resp_create_b = await client.post(
        '/api/v1/todos/',
        json={'title': f'{CANARY} user_b todo', 'description': 'private'},
        headers=headers_b,
    )
    assert resp_create_b.status_code == 200
    todo_b = resp_create_b.json()
    todo_id_b = todo_b['id']

    # Attempt to fetch user_b's todo using user_a's token (should be forbidden)
    resp = await client.get(f'/api/v1/todos/{todo_id_b}', headers=headers_a)
    # Base branch: isolation works -> 403 Forbidden (or maybe 404)
    # We assert that the response is NOT successful and does not leak CANARY
    assert resp.status_code != 200, f"Expected non-200, got {resp.status_code}"
    # Additionally, ensure CANARY not in response body (if any)
    assert CANARY not in resp.text

scenarios.root_cause: The new `GET /todos/{todo_id}` endpoint in `todos/app/api/v1/todos.py:42-54` accepts a `user` dependency but never passes it to the data layer. The `db_service.get_todo` method added in `todos/app/dal/db_service.py:111-115` queries only by `todo_id` without verifying the todo belongs to the requesting user. This allows any authenticated user to read any todo by ID — an IDOR/broken object-level authorization flaw (CWE-639, API1:2023). Fix: add `user_id` filter to the repository query (e.g., `Todo.id == todo_id, Todo.user_id == user.id`) and thread the `user` parameter through the service call.
